name: vwap_mean_reversion_5s_5
author: adapted from quant_system
thesis: Exploits short-term overreaction away from VWAP in liquid FnO stocks. Institutional algorithms anchor to VWAP for execution benchmarks, creating a gravitational pull back to VWAP after deviations. The inefficiency persists because retail participants chase momentum on deviations while institutional flow reverts price. Capacity-limited (can't move size without eating your edge) which protects it from full arbitrage.
mechanism: Short-term selling exhausts available demand at a price level, creating a temporary liquidity vacuum. Market makers who absorbed the selling begin marking prices back to reduce inventory risk. Limit buy orders resting below create a floor, and new participants entering the long side accelerate the reversion as the forced selling pressure dissipates.

filters.volume_filter: skip if bar volume < 50% of 20-bar SMA(volume)
filters.expiry_filter: skip on monthly expiry day and RBI policy day

weaknesses: Fails in strong trending days — deviation from VWAP is justified, not mean-reverting. Need trend filter or VIX spike cutoff to avoid catching knives.
High VIX regimes (>22) widen the distribution of deviations, making fixed z-score thresholds unreliable. The 2.0 zscore cutoff may fire too early in volatile regimes.
Slippage increases sharply on fast reversals — the same move that triggers entry attracts other mean-reversion algos, front-running the fill.
prior_art: Classic VWAP reversion. Widely documented in institutional execution literature. Edge here is in the confirmation filter (bounce + RSI + volume) not the core idea.
adaptation_notes: Converted from 1min to 5s bars. Lookback multiplier: 12x. Adaptations: timeframe scaling to 5-second candles; apply to NIFTY/BANKNIFTY index instead of FnO universe; lookback period scaling for 5-second bars; stop/target recalibration for 5-second timeframe. Stop/target calibrated for options point-based exits. Universe narrowed to NIFTY index.
